newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CYCLING-MUSEEUW CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY WITH ROAD RACE GOLD.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-MUSEEUW CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY WITH ROAD RACE GOLD.

text.p: Belgian Johan Museeuw celebrated his 31st birthday in style by winning the world elite men's road race title on Sunday.
His final sprint ruined hopes of a home-town triumph as he beat Lugano-born Mauro Gianetti after they had led for the final 30 of the 252-km race over a challenging course.
Michele Bartoli snatched the bronze for Italy, holding off Belgian Axel Merckx, the son of Eddy Merckx who won the last of his three world titles 22 years ago.
Museeuw said: "I was always scared of what might happen because there were a lot of good riders in our leading group. However, I felt really strong and always held a little in reserve."
A week ago he said his season was finished but he changed his mind 48 hours later.
It was Belgium's first road-race title since 1990 when Rudy Dhaenens took the gold at Utsunomiya, Japan, with compatriot Dirk de Wolf second.
Museeuw had an edgy time in the final two kilometres. With Gianetti shadowing him the Belgian kept turning in his saddle, inviting the Swiss rider to come forward and take up the pace.
Gianetti declined and the Belgian camp's nerves were taut as they realised the pursuers were closing in and the leaders were coasting.
When Gianetti did make a move in the finishing straight it was not powerful enough and Museeuw's response settled the race by one second. Bronze medallist Bartoli finished 29 seconds later.

Gianetti said: "I wanted to give my marvellous public a big gift -- the title. In the final kilometres I told Museeuw that he had to work now because I had done most of the work on the climbs. However, he was stronger and I was too tired."
Museeuw engineered the decisive escape as an original breakaway of 12 fell apart under constant pressure on the two major climbs.

Only Gianetti could match the Belgian whose attack on the slopes of Comano left the remaining co-leaders to be gathered in by the advancing Bartoli, Merckx, Frenchman Richard Virenque and Italian Andrea Tafi.
Benoit Salmon of France and Andrei Zinchenko of Russia set the early pace with a breakaway of more than 100 kms during which they built an advantage of three minutes and 20 seconds.
Then, with less than 100 kms remaining, 12 riders escaped to establish a lead which grew to three minutes before the group dwindled to seven.
Alex Zuelle, the first of Switzerland's two world champions over the last four days, crashed after 151 kms. A feeding bag held out by a helper hit his handlebars and the Swiss racer fell heavily.
Zuelle, the world time-trial number one, retired from Sunday's race with a lump on his head and a grazed knee.
